cards.text: Abraham's visitors get up to leave, and they look out over the city of Sodom. Abraham walks along with them to see them off. These days most of us see a guest off by yelling "BYE" from the couch, so give this man some credit.
Then the LORD asks, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?" Friend, when you hear a line like THAT, you put the cookie down and you lean in.

cards.question: The LORD says Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation. Through him, all the nations of the earth will be ___.
True or false: The LORD says He chose Abraham so Abraham would command his children and his household to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about two cities, Sodom and Gomorrah. The outcry against them is great, and their sin is so grievous.

cards.question: With an outcry that great against Sodom and Gomorrah, what does the LORD say He will do?

answers.text: Go down and see if their actions fit the outcry
Send a messenger to warn them one more time
Leave the two cities alone until next year

cards.text: The two men turn away and head toward Sodom, but Abraham stays right there, standing before the LORD. Everybody else is leaving, and Abraham is planted like a man with one more thing to say.

cards.question: Abraham steps forward to speak to the LORD. What does he ask?

answers.text: Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked
Will You really send a warning to the wicked first
Will You really let me walk down with the two men

cards.text: Then Abraham puts a number out there: what if there are fifty righteous people in the city, will the LORD still sweep it away and not spare the place for their sake? Friend, most of us can't even talk our way out of a late fee, and Abraham is making his case to the LORD Himself!

cards.question: True or false: Abraham tells the LORD it would be fine for the righteous and the wicked to be treated alike.

cards.text: Then Abraham says, "Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" That's a BOLD question, friend, and he asks it with his whole chest.

cards.question: The LORD answers Abraham about fifty righteous people in Sodom. What will the LORD do if He finds them?

answers.text: Spare the whole place on their account
Rescue the fifty and let the city fall
Give the city one more year to change

cards.text: Abraham speaks up again, and this time he calls himself "dust and ashes". Friend, I spent YEARS covered in junk drawer dust, and Abraham still out-humbled me.

cards.question: Abraham asks what happens if the fifty righteous people are five short. True or false: The LORD says if He finds forty-five there, He will not destroy the city.

cards.text: Abraham asks about forty, and the LORD says on account of the forty He won't do it. Then Abraham says, "May the Lord not be angry," and he goes down to thirty.

cards.question: True or false: When Abraham asks about thirty righteous people in Sodom, the LORD says thirty isn't enough to spare the city.
After thirty, Abraham speaks to the Lord again and goes lower. What number of righteous people does he ask about next?

cards.text: The LORD answers that on account of the twenty, He will not destroy it. Fifty, forty-five, forty, thirty, TWENTY, friend, this man is working those numbers like a clearance rack on the last day of the sale!

cards.question: Abraham says, "May the Lord not be angry," and says he'll speak just once more. He asks what if only ___ righteous people are found in Sodom.

cards.text: The LORD answers, "On account of the ten, I will not destroy it." Then He departs, Abraham heads home, and friend, keep that apron on, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: "Everybody else is leaving" contradicts the text. In Genesis 18:22 only the two men turn away toward Sodom. The LORD stays, and Abraham remains standing before Him. The same card even says Abraham is "standing before the LORD." This line is part of the retelling, not an exaggeration inside a joke, so it states something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke compares the exchange to "a clearance rack on the last day of the sale." In that picture, the LORD's answers to Abraham's intercession become a store marking down its prices, so the humor lands on God's mercy and not only on Abraham's human situation. The comparison also doesn't match the core action. Abraham is asking about fewer and fewer righteous people, but a clearance rack is the seller lowering prices.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.
